selectionNotes: Select Marciniak et al. (2009) convex model 169 (125,-33); alternate 170 (308,-41) remains. The publication concerns light-curve-derived spin/shape. The selected record has no calibrated size and supplies no registered imagery; retain explicitly approximate AKARI scaling.
sourceLimitations: The pinned mesh is an inverse model, not a directly sampled surface. No registered reflectance mosaic is supplied by this release; a neutral grid must mark unavailable imagery. Fine-scale craters, regolith and albedo are unresolved. Absolute rotational phase is illustrative. Select Marciniak et al. (2009) convex model 169 (125,-33); alternate 170 (308,-41) remains. The publication concerns light-curve-derived spin/shape. The selected record has no calibrated size and supplies no registered imagery; retain explicitly approximate AKARI scaling.
calibrationSelection: Pinned AKARI AcuA v1.0 thermal effective-sphere diameter is assigned to mesh volume only as an explicit display-scale approximation; formal catalog errors omit additional shape, spin and thermal-model systematics.
sourceCoordinatePreservation: Original counted shape bytes, coordinates, vertex order, face order and one-based connectivity are retained unchanged. One preparation-owned uniform scale maps original coordinates to km.

visibleShapeDescription: Convex light-curve reconstruction with approximate thermal size: 77.72 km (catalog ±1.23 km; additional shape and thermal-model uncertainty). Thermal size is used as a volume-scale approximation. An alternative pole remains possible. The grid marks unavailable imagery.

calibration.uncertaintyKind: Formal catalog uncertainty; excludes extra shape, spin and thermal-model systematics. It is not the total uncertainty of the displayed physical scale.
calibration.additionalSystematics: Usui2011§2.3 explicitly omits unquantified shape/spin/thermal-model effects; rotation can add a few to about10%in size, especially for fewdetections. No invented numerical confidence interval is assigned to these unquantified effects.
calibration.diameterSemantics: Mean fitted diameter of a nonrotating sphere in the modified Standard Thermal Model. Its use as the volume-equivalent diameter of the separate convex DAMIT mesh is an explicit display-scale approximation, not a published physical-volume calibration.
calibration.limitations: The physical size is approximately calibrated by assigning the AKARI thermal effective diameter to the mesh volume-equivalent diameter. Neither source mesh nor spin is modified. Convex inversion supplies only broad outline; no resolved craters, concavities, reflectance or regolith texture can be inferred. Select Marciniak et al. (2009) convex model 169 (125,-33); alternate 170 (308,-41) remains. The publication concerns light-curve-derived spin/shape.
